comment: Which capture readers blind-tester/run.sh has an actual LAUNCH PATH written against.
This is deliberately separate from the registry's `capture` block, because they answer
two different questions and both have to be true before a vendor can play live:
registry capture block -> 'a reader exists that can PROVE this vendor's blindness'
this file              -> 'run.sh knows how to SPAWN this vendor in the first place'
Landing a reader without a launch path is the dangerous half. The derived gate would
open, and run.sh would fall through to the Codex launch and execute
`codex exec --model <the other vendor's model>` — a burned launch recorded under the
wrong vendor's name. That is why run.sh checks this list too, and why the list names
READER MODULES rather than provider ids: the launch path is written against a reader's
requirements (where its log lives, how the session id is obtained), not against a brand.
bin/doctor.ts reads this same file so its table cannot promise a live lane that run.sh
would refuse. Adding a vendor is: registry entry + capture block + reader module +
a launch branch in run.sh + one line here. The first three make the evidence honest;
the last two make it runnable.
